observations.answer:
I wrote the QA plan into the ledger before running anything, then ran one session that took about 15 minutes. The session confirmed the cause of the incident: `textstats.chunk` silently drops the last, shorter batch.

## The plan
I added the ledger at `.agentic-qa/` and recorded the plan as session `qa-2026-10-29-chunk-postmortem`, at revision `755629a` with no local changes. It has two parts:
1. **Does `chunk()` keep every item?** Ten specific cases, including exactly 100 items, 101 and 99 items in batches of 50, fewer items than one batch, empty input, a generator, the README example, and a sweep over many lengths and batch sizes. The expected answers come from the docstring and README ("the last one may be shorter"), not from reading the code.
2. **Why didn't the tests catch it?** This answers the postmortem's first action item.

## What I checked
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Existing test suite | All 5 tests pass |
| What the `chunk` tests cover | Only one positive test, with 4 items in batches of 2. That is the one kind of input where the bug can't show. |
| Check script, run from a scratch folder outside the repo | 101 items → 100 come out; 99 → 50; 3 → none; README example gives `[[1, 2]]` instead of `[[1, 2], [3]]`. In the sweep, 1,187 of 1,573 length/size pairs lose items, and the number lost is always the leftover (`n % size`). |
| Same failure rerun twice in fresh processes | Identical both times; it always happens |

## Findings (both confirmed)
- **High:** `chunk()` drops the trailing `n % size` items without any error. With batches of 50 that is 1–49 items per run, which matches the postmortem.
- **Medium:** the tests never use a length that isn't a multiple of the batch size, so they passed before and after the incident.

I closed the session with the decision **"hold"**: on this revision, the evidence doesn't support moving the export back to batches of 50. The ledger validates, and all 7 evidence files are in `.agentic-qa/sessions/qa-2026-10-29-chunk-postmortem/evidence/`.

## What I didn't check, and why
- **The fix and new tests:** changing `src/` or `tests/` needs your approval, so I made no changes. I haven't suggested any code change, and the cause is recorded as "unknown".
- **The export job and indexer:** they aren't in this repository. I tied the bug to the incident by matching the symptom, not by running the export.
- **Which documents need re-exporting, and other code that calls `chunk()`:** that would need export or production data, which I haven't been authorised to use. I also left the customer details from the postmortem out of the ledger.
- **Other environments and wider testing:** I only ran Python 3.13.16. I didn't install a property-testing library, so the sweep was a fixed grid of lengths 0–120 and sizes 1–12 plus 50.
- **`word_counts` and `top_words`:** these only ran as part of the existing tests.

The `.agentic-qa/` folder is not committed yet. The next most useful step, once approved, is to fix `chunk()`, add tests that fail on `755629a`, and rerun the saved check script against the fix. Separately, the export should check how many items went in against how many were sent, because "sent N batches" in its logs can't show that items were dropped.

observations.answer:
I found the cause of the incident: `textstats.chunk` never sends the last batch when it has fewer than `size` items. With a batch size of 50, any run whose length isn't a multiple of 50 silently drops its last 1–49 items, which is exactly what the postmortem describes. The tests passed because they never try a length that doesn't divide evenly. My recommendation is not to go back to batches of 50 on this revision.

**Plan recorded first.** I set up the QA ledger in `.agentic-qa/` and recorded the plan (session `qa-chunk-postmortem-2026-10-29`, revision `ad70600`, clean tree) before running anything. It had two parts: check whether `chunk` keeps every item, and find out why the tests missed it. I left the customer details in the postmortem out of the ledger.

**What I checked** (Python 3.13.16, made-up test data only, about 15 minutes):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Existing tests (the command in the README) | Pass, 5/5. The only `chunk` test with data splits 4 items into batches of 2, so there's never a leftover. |
| The README's own example `list(chunk([1,2,3],2))` | Fail: returns `[[1, 2]]`, should be `[[1, 2], [3]]` |
| Batch size 50 with 100 / 101 / 149 / 49 items | 100 is fine. 101 loses 1 item, 149 loses 49, and 49 items produce no batch at all. |
| Generator input (7 items, size 3) | Fail: loses 1 item |
| Empty input | Pass |
| Identical rerun | Same output, so the failure is consistent every time |

- **Finding (confirmed, high severity):** `finding-chunk-drops-tail`. From reading the code (I didn't change anything to prove it), `src/textstats/core.py:31-36` only sends a batch once it's full. Nothing sends the leftover items after the loop ends.
- **First postmortem action item ("why didn't the tests catch this?"):** the only `chunk` test with data uses a length that divides evenly by the batch size, and nothing checks that every input item comes out the other end.

**What I couldn't check:**
- **The export job, the indexer, and the "sent N batches" logging:** none of these are in this repository. The link to the incident rests on the postmortem's description, not on running the export.
- **Other Python versions:** only 3.13.16 was available.
- **`word_counts` and `top_words`:** only covered by the existing tests, since they weren't the incident risk.

**Where I stopped:** before anything that needs your go-ahead. That covers fixing `chunk`, adding a regression test, filing a backlog item, and contacting the export owners. The ledger also notes a risk worth raising with them: anything else using `chunk` may have been losing items since 2026-09-02.

The ledger validates with all 7 evidence files present; they're in `.agentic-qa/sessions/qa-chunk-postmortem-2026-10-29/evidence/`. The only change to the repo is the new, uncommitted `.agentic-qa/` folder, after I removed the `__pycache__` folders my test run created. The next step I'd suggest is approving a fix plus a regression test that covers leftover batches, then rerunning the saved check script to confirm.

I've recorded the plan in the QA ledger as session `qa-2026-10-29-chunk-remainder`, at status `planned`. No checks were run: not the test suite, not any probe of `chunk()`.

**Where:** `.agentic-qa/manifest.json` (new) and the session file next to it, pinned to revision `1193780`, which was clean.

## What I planned

From reading the code, I suspect a cause, but nothing has tested it yet. `chunk()` in `src/textstats/core.py` builds each batch and hands it over only once it holds exactly `size` items. Nothing hands over the leftover batch when the input runs out. That fits the postmortem: the missing documents were always at the end of the run, and between 1 and 49 of them at a batch size of 50. The only batching test, `test_even_split`, uses 4 items in batches of 2, so there's never a leftover. The README's own example, `chunk([1, 2, 3], 2)` giving `[[1, 2], [3]]`, has no matching test.

The plan has two parts:

1. **Leftover and edge cases for `chunk()`** (15 min, 6 attempts). Each case is compared against the result of plainly slicing the input into groups:
   - the README example
   - 51 items in batches of 50 (one left over)
   - 99 items in batches of 50 (49 left over)
   - exactly 100 items (no empty extra batch)
   - fewer items than one batch
   - empty input
   - a generator as input rather than a list
   - a sweep over input lengths 0–120 and batch sizes 1, 2, 3, 49, 50 and 51, checking every item comes out once, in order
   - batch size 0 or negative raises an error

   If the slicing result is contradicted, the plan stops and moves to confirming the defect rather than widening the scope.
2. **Why the tests missed it** (10 min, 2 attempts). Run the existing suite once with the README command to get a baseline, then check each promise in the docstring and README against the tests. A passing suite counts only as a baseline, not as proof that `chunk()` is correct.

## What I could not establish

- **Whether the bug is real.** That needs the checks you told me not to run yet.
- **Anything about the export job or the indexer.** They aren't in this repository, so I can't tell whether `chunk()` is the only cause. For example, I can't see whether the job also checks how many documents it sent.
- **Which Python version the export uses.** I recorded the version on this machine (3.13.16) for planning only; it should be recorded again when the checks run.

## Authority still needed

- **Small test scripts.** Running the existing suite is a normal local check, but the edge cases need short `python -c` commands or a scratch script outside the repo. Please confirm those count as local checks.
- **Adding a test or fixing `chunk()`.** That would change source and tests, which needs separate approval. The plan doesn't include it.
- **Customer details.** The postmortem names a customer and their email. I kept those out of the ledger, and the plan uses made-up test data only.

The ledger rejected my first write because of an invalid quality-attribute name. I corrected the name and the second write was accepted. Planning took well under the 20-minute budget.

In `src/textstats/core.py:31-36`, `chunk()` only yields a batch when it is full, so a final partial batch is never sent. That contradicts its own docstring ("the last one may be shorter") and the README example, where `chunk([1,2,3], 2)` gives `[[1, 2], [3]]`.
- **Why the tests missed it:** `tests/test_core.py` only checks a list that splits evenly and a size of zero. No test has leftover items, so the existing checks could not have seen the failure. The unit tests are where this should have been caught.

## The plan: three test plans ("charters"), 13 specific checks, about 45 minutes in total
1. **Regression test using the incident as the expected result** (15 min). Feed in 51, 99, 3 and 0 items with a batch size of 50, plus 100 items (an exact multiple), single-item batches (the current workaround), generator input and the README example. The test passes only if putting all the batches back together gives exactly the original list, in order.
2. **Why the suite missed it** (20 min). This answers the postmortem's first action item. One check tries many list lengths and batch sizes and confirms no item is lost, duplicated or reordered. The other checks whether the existing tests can tell the shipped `chunk()` apart from a correct version at all.
3. **The same gap in the other helpers** (10 min). The edge cases for `top_words` and `word_counts` (asking for zero words, asking for more words than exist, empty text) aren't tested either.

## What I could not establish
- **Whether `chunk()` really drops the last batch.** This comes from reading the code only. Confirming it means running checks, which you asked me not to do yet.
- **The export job.** Its code, its logs and the indexer aren't in this repository. I can't confirm that the export calls `chunk()` the way the postmortem describes, or that nothing else contributed. Looking at production logs, support tickets or monitoring would need separate approval.
- **Whether going back to batches of 50 is safe.** That depends on the results of plans 1 and 2, and on a fix that is outside QA's scope.
- **How words with accents or digits should be counted.** The documentation doesn't say, so I logged it as an open question for plan 3, not as a defect.

## Where I stopped
- **Running the plan needs your go-ahead.** That means running the local tests and adding temporary test cases.
- **Fixing `chunk()` needs a separate request.**
- **Customer details stay out.** The postmortem names a customer, with an email and account number. I kept those out of the ledger and checked that none of them appear in it.

observations.answer:
I've recorded the plan in the QA ledger as session `qa-escape-chunk-2026-10-29` (status `planned`). No checks were run and no product code was changed. The ledger is new: I created it at `.agentic-qa/` in the repo, and its validation passes. It is untracked; I haven't committed it.

## What the incident teaches
- **What went wrong:** after the nightly export switched to batches of 50 on 2026-09-02, each run silently left out the last 1–49 documents. The tests passed both before and after the change.
- **Likely cause, still present now:** from reading `src/textstats/core.py:26`, `chunk()` never sends the leftover partial batch at the end. The README's own example (`chunk([1, 2, 3], 2)` → `[[1, 2], [3]]`) would come out as just `[[1, 2]]`. I haven't run anything, so this is a suspected defect, not a confirmed one.
- **Why the tests missed it:** `tests/test_core.py` only tries inputs that divide evenly (4 items in batches of 2) and a batch size of 0. No test ever has items left over, and nothing checks that the README examples actually hold.

## Planned round (3 charters, 11 test points, about 35 minutes)
1. **Regression test for the leftover batch (unit tests, the layer that should have caught it).** Uses the README example and batches of 50 with 51, 99, 100, 3 and 0 items, plus a one-pass generator of 51 items. It passes only if all batches joined together equal the input, in order. On the first lost item it stops and goes to reproduction, without fixing.
2. **Check that no item is ever lost.** Covers every combination of 0–120 items and batch sizes 1–60, plus 500 random cases with a fixed seed, using only the standard library. It checks that nothing is lost, duplicated or reordered, and that the batch count and sizes are right. This matters because the export logged "sent N batches" with no errors, so nothing downstream would notice.
3. **Can the existing tests catch this at all?** This answers the postmortem's "why did the tests not catch this" item. It runs the README test command once to see whether it finds all 5 tests. It also checks whether the current suite fails on code that drops the leftover batch. Any change for that check would be made in a scratch copy, never in the repo.

## What I could not establish, and why
- **How the export job uses `chunk()`:** the job isn't in this repo, so I can't confirm it calls `chunk()` directly with a batch size of 50.
- **Which textstats version ran during the incident:** git history has only one commit. I can only show the cause exists at the current commit (`9f445fb`), and only by reading the code.
- **Which checks gated the 2026-09-02 change:** the repo has no CI configuration.
- **Production data:** I used only the postmortem. Logs, export runs, monitoring and support tickets each need separate approval, so I didn't touch them. I left the customer's personal details in the postmortem out of the ledger.
- **Python version:** not checked, because that would mean running something.
- **`word_counts` and `top_words`:** left out of this round, since the incident says nothing about them.

## Where I stopped
Running the charters needs your go-ahead. That covers the local unit-test command and the scratch-copy check in charter 3. Fixing `chunk()` is a separate decision. Deciding whether the export can go back to batches of 50 belongs to whoever owns it, not to this QA round.
